data readiness
A proposed common language of banded levels (A, B, C with numbered sub-levels) for assessing and communicating the readiness of a data set for analysis.
data accessibility band
The band of data readiness concerned with the accessibility of a data set, including verification of existence, format, privacy, legal, ethical and topological constraints.
faithfulness and representation band

The band of data readiness concerned with the faithfulness and representation of the data once loaded into software: missing values, noise, entry errors, units, and collection-process characteristics.
data in context band
The band of data readiness concerned with data in context: the appropriateness of a data set to answer a particular question or support a particular analysis, requiring a defined task.
C4
Data whose existence is asserted but unverified; the lowest sub-level (C4) of Band C.
The top of Band C: data ready to load into analysis software or share, machine readable, with ethical procedures for data handling addressed.
The top of Band B: the analyst has a broad idea of the limitations of the data and how faithful it is to its description.
The top of Band A: data considered alongside a defined task with remedial steps taken, ready to be deployed in the given context.
The quality of a data set, argued to require as much control and measurement as model quality.
